current.text: Fred VanVleet is back, so Thompson moves off point guard and plays less of the lead ball handler role.
He is a projected starter next to VanVleet, Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Sengun.
Experts expect the role change to cost him about one assist per game. They expect his blocks to come back toward 0.9, his steals to rise a little and his FG% to reach 55 or 56%.

Most experts call him a second-round player in category leagues. Lloyd's newest call: mid-to-late second round if his blocks and FG% improve, otherwise a third-round pick around 28 to 30. He calls ESPN's rank of 13 slightly aggressive.
In an auction mock, Josh valued him at about 40 USD. He went for 35 USD, which Josh did not call an overpay.
Ime Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes.
With our March 28 end, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule: 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: Thompson is an elite athlete who does not make threes.
He is an efficient inside scorer, and his FG% is high for a guard.
He is a low scorer for his draft range and is unlikely to average 20 points.
Blocks drive his value. He gives rim deterrence on defense, and he gets fewer blocks when he plays point guard.
His rebounds, steals and blocks are strong for a guard. Threes are his only clearly weak category.
He is worth clearly more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: The experts value him at 35 to 40 USD. That is between Yahoo's average cost of 29.8 USD and ESPN's 37.4 USD, and close to the 38 USD he went for in our league last season. Bidding up to the high 30s is fair, but Lloyd says he is a third-round pick (about 28 to 30) if his blocks and FG% do not come back. He fits punt 3PM builds best. He helps in FG%, REB, STL and BLK for a guard, but Houston's 10-game playoff schedule is a drawback. In the first weeks, check whether his blocks get back near 0.9 and his FG% gets near 55% now that he is off point guard. Also check how much his 5 assists drop.
